source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Work done by driving force up a hill at constant speed

hints: At constant speed, work done by driving force equals gain in potential energy plus work against resistance: $W = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resist}}$.

walkthrough.text:

$$\Delta E_p = mg d\sin\theta = (1200)(10)(80)(0.05) = 48000\text{ J} = 48\text{ kJ}$$
$$W_{\text{resist}} = R d = (600)(80) = 48000\text{ J} = 48\text{ kJ}$$

Apply the work-energy principle for constant speed (zero change in kinetic energy):
$$W_{\text{driving}} = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resist}} = 48000 + 48000 = 96000\text{ J} = 96\text{ kJ}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify energy requirements:
- Climbing requires lifting mass against gravity and overcoming drag:
$$\Delta E_p = 48000\text{ J}, \quad W_{\text{drag}} = 48000\text{ J}$$

Sum total work needed:
- Adding potential gain and drag work:
$$W = 48 + 48 = 96\text{ kJ}$$
The driving force performs $96\text{ kJ}$ of work.

Obtains total work done $W = 48000 + 48000 = 96000\text{ J} = 96\text{ kJ}$.
